title: Temporal Smart Notes Preserve What Was True at a Given Time
summary: Every durable Smart Note carries timezone-aware timestamps and explicit supersession relationships so Naya can distinguish current truth from historical truth and reconstruct what was believed or established at an earlier time.
what_happened: The design explicitly required dated and timestamped notes so changing decisions are not lost and users can intentionally return to earlier states.
what_we_learned: History should be preserved rather than silently rewritten.
A superseded decision can remain useful as historical context.
Temporal retrieval is required for trustworthy continuity when architecture or assumptions change.
why_it_matters: Without temporal provenance, memory can create false currentness and make old decisions look like present truth.
what_changed: The memory schema requires created_at and effective_at.
The retrieval manifest defines historical and supersession behavior.
next_best_action: Add temporal retrieval tests for current, historical, superseded, and conflicting notes.
evidence: Explicit user requirement and architecture decision recorded 2026-08-23
